findings.desc: Claude CLI executability audit found real executable criteria gaps: Lattice-Engineering-baseline.md uses undefined required_engineering_runs and undefined overall_correctness_protected_success_rate / weighted success-rate formula, while Lattice-Production-Safety-baseline.md makes requiredIndependentHosts conditional with "when configured". These gaps can let teams pass or authorize baselines without a mechanically defined minimum run count, metric formula, or hard multi-host requirement.

Codex CLI coverage audit found real baseline coverage gaps: PROD-SOAK-1 requires duration but no production-stage minimum valid run count/cadence, and UDM-HUMAN-HANDOFF-1 can pass by emitting handoff-shaped artifacts without proving a human-required decision blocks DONE and resumes only with human evidence. These gaps can let a suite pass while the claimed safety or handoff behavior is false.

Codex CLI claim-boundary audit found that the Claim Baseline Suite table allowed-claim wording is broader than the detailed allowed wording: Loop Engineering omits the tested task class boundary, and Production Safety omits the stated maturity target boundary. Because this table is a structured claim authorization surface, it could be quoted as authorizing broader claims than the evidence supports.
